text:
jessica: FYI customer ticket #C-4821 — large SaaS customer on Dedicated (tenant t-9342) seeing spikes of 429s and very high tail latency starting ~2026-03-17T14:20Z. They say pool shows healthy GPU usage in Console but responses routed slowly and many requests get throttled.

ops-bot: New ticket assigned to #support: C-4821 (priority P1) — triggered by 429 rate.

jessica: Quick summary from the customer: requests to /v1/generate get 429 with header `x-rate-limit-reason:_pool_throttled`. They shared curl output with headers: 
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-rate-limit-reason: pool_throttled
x-pool-id: shared-burst-7
x-tenant-id: t-9342
retry-after: 3
```
They expect x-pool-id to be `dedicated-west-3:dp-42` (their dedicated pool).

oncall-marc: ack — pinging eng-platform and eng-runtime. Do we have any control plane deploys or config rolls around 14:10-14:18Z?

natalie: I see a control-plane config sync at 14:12Z — a thin migration that renamed tier aliases (internal refactor). Change was to map `tier:gold` -> `dedicated:dp-*` via alias table. The migration had a fallback clause added: `if alias_missing -> map to shared-burst`. That fallback is new.

sre-jen: That's suspicious — if the alias lookup fails for that tenant, routing will pick the fallback shared pool which is rate limited per-tenant and could cause 429s. Can customer confirm the tenant's tier label?

jessica: Customer provided: `tier: gold-enterprise` (custom alias created during onboarding). Their alias should have been matched to dp-42. Looks like the migration changed exact-match logic to prefix-match only, so `gold-enterprise` isn't matching `gold`.

eng-qa: Repro steps I ran from a repro script (local):
```
# expected path -> dedicated
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test" -H "X-Tenant-ID: t-9342" \
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hi"}'
# got 429 and header x-pool-id: shared-burst-7
```
Logs from the router: `route_lookup(t-9342): alias_lookup("gold-enterprise") -> not_found -> fallback: shared-burst-7`

natalie: Confirmed: the alias table migration used a new normalizer that strips suffixes but only for exact matches; custom suffixes created during onboarding were not present in the new table. This is a control-plane logic regression.

oncall-marc: Immediate mitigation options? 1) Roll back migration, 2) Patch alias resolver to do longest-prefix match for existing tenant aliases, 3) Add a safe fallback to route to tenant's pinned pool if present.

jessica: Customer is impacted (production). They need a fix now, rollback preferred. Billing is worried about churn.

billing-liaison: Customer reports billing anomalies due to retries and 429s triggering additional requests; will open a billing credit draft after we confirm duration.

sre-jen: I'm pushing a hot rollback of the migration to the control plane (config-service) now — will report back when finished.

ops-bot: Deploy started: config-service rollback (user: sre-jen) — id: deploy-ccf-20260317-01.

sre-jen: Rollback completed at 2026-03-17T14:28Z. Re-ran test:
```
# after rollback
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-test" -H "X-Tenant-ID: t-9342" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -d '{"input":"hi"}'
# HTTP/1.1 200 OK
# x-pool-id: dedicated-west-3:dp-42
```
Customer confirms traffic is now landing on dp-42 and 429s stopped.

natalie: Root cause: alias migration changed matching semantics (exact->prefix-only) and added an unsafe fallback to shared pools. Regression introduced in commit `a5f4d2c` during the control-plane refactor.

eng-qa: Suggested postmortem items:
- Add unit tests for alias matching semantics (exact + suffix cases)
- Remove silent fallback to burst pools for dedicated-tenants (require explicit mapping)
- Add alert when large number of tenants switch pool mapping within 1 minute
- Add automated tenant-level observability: show alias->pool mapping diffs in Console.

jessica: Customer asked for timeline and credit. We gave them ETA: fix rolled back at 14:28Z, root-cause analysis in progress, will propose a goodwill credit for the 8 minute window and any downstream retries.

oncall-marc: Also note we should check autoscaler logs — if many tenants moved to shared pool at once it may have triggered aggressive scale-down/scale-up and noisy neighbor throttling. I see a matching spike in shared-burst metrics 14:18-14:25Z.

natalie: Agreed. I'll follow up with an action item: revert the normalization change and harden the alias migration script. I'll file an ENG-PLAT ticket with PR to revert plus tests.

eng-qa: Quick repro commands for triage team (useful in future):
```
# dump routing lookup result for a tenant
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-admin" https://controlplane.internal/v1/route/lookup?t=t-9342
# expect: {"tenant":"t-9342","alias":"gold-enterprise","pool":"dedicated-west-3:dp-42"}
# migration bug returned: {"tenant":"t-9342","alias":"gold-enterprise","pool":"shared-burst-7"}
```

sre-jen: Will open postmortem and link PRs. Also add a temporary monitoring rule: alert if >5% of requests for dedicated-tenants are routed to shared pools in 1m window.

jessica: Customer updated on action and accepts credit offer, will monitor for 24h. Closing ticket once we confirm no regressions. :thumbsup:

ops-bot: Ticket C-4821 status: mitigated -> monitoring.

natalie: Final notes for postmortem: cause = control-plane alias normalization + unsafe fallback; impact = unintended throttling & noisy-neighbor tail latency; fix = rollback + revert logic + tests + improved alerts. ETA for full patch to prevent recurrence: 48h.

eng-qa: I'll add test vectors and a small harness for alias edgecases.

jessica: Thanks team — keep updates here if customer sees anything else.
